raw.question: European country agrees to give Ukraine security guarantee by December 31?
raw.description:

A qualifying “security guarantee” requires language that is equivalent in character to a NATO Article 5–style mutual defense commitment: the relevant European country must commit to responding militarily if Ukraine is attacked, or otherwise guarantee Ukraine’s defense through binding defense obligations. Examples of qualifying language include commitments modeled on the US treaties with Japan, South Korea, or the Philippines, or NATO's Article 5 instrument, which obligates the United States to “act to meet the common danger” through military force if an ally is attacked. A qualifying agreement must be jointly announced and finalized, and take the form of a treaty, executive agreement, memorandum of understanding, joint declaration, or equivalent written instrument. This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 8 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/cn/shenzhen/ZGSZ.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecast models for Shenzhen point to a daily high in the mid-30s Celsius on August 8 as the dominant outcome, with traders assigning the highest implied probabilities to 35–37 °C. Subtropical high pressure, elevated solar insolation, and southerly monsoon flow typically drive peak temperatures near 31–33 °C in early August, yet recent days have shown readings climbing into the mid-30s amid above-average humidity that limits nocturnal cooling. Sea-breeze moderation from the Pearl River estuary and any residual cloud cover from regional moisture can cap extremes, while the absence of an active typhoon or heat-dome setup keeps probabilities away from 38 °C or higher. Updated numerical guidance and local meteorological agency briefings expected within the next 24 hours will refine these ranges ahead of market resolution.
